turns.question: Where is middleware composition implemented?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the hono repository's middleware composition implementation using gh CLI.Found `src/compose.ts` — that's almost certainly it. Let me read it and check how it's used in `hono-base.ts`.I have everything needed. Let me also quickly check the router's `match` return shape to confirm what feeds into `compose`, and check `types.ts` for `COMPOSED_HANDLER` context.I now have a complete picture. Here's the answer:

## Middleware composition in Hono

### Core implementation: `src/compose.ts`

The `compose` function (`src/compose.ts:19`) is the heart of it — a Koa-style middleware composer (explicitly documented as "based on the `koa-compose` package"):

```ts
export const compose = <E extends Env = Env>(
  middleware: [[Function, unknown], unknown][] | [[Function]][],
  onError?: ErrorHandler<E>,
  onNotFound?: NotFoundHandler<E>
): ((context: Context, next?: Next) => Promise<Context>) => { ... }
```

- It returns a function `(context, next) => Promise<Context>`.
- Internally it uses a recursive `dispatch(i)` closure that calls `middleware[i][0][0]` (the handler) with `context` and a `next` callback bound to `() => dispatch(i + 1)` — the classic "onion" middleware model where each handler can run code before/after calling `next()`.
- Guards against calling `next()` more than once via the `index`/`i <= index` check, throwing `'next() called multiple times'`.
- Catches errors thrown by handlers and routes them to `onError` if provided (setting `context.error` and marking `isError`); otherwise rethrows.
- If no more middleware and no `next`, falls back to `onNotFound`.
- Sets `context.res` from a handler's return value only if `context.finalized === false` (or if it's an error result).

### Where it's invoked: `src/hono-base.ts`

- `#dispatch()` (`src/hono-base.ts`, private method) is the request-handling core called from `.fetch()`. It matches routes via `this.router.match(method, path)`, producing `matchResult[0]` — an array of `[handler, RouterRoute]` tuples for every middleware/handler registered on the matched path.
  - **Fast path optimization**: if `matchResult[0].length === 1` (only one handler matched, i.e., no middleware stack), it calls the handler directly without invoking `compose` at all — this is called out explicitly in a comment: `// Do not 'compose' if it has only one handler`.
  - Otherwise: `const composed = compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)`, then `await composed(c)` runs the full chain, and the resulting `context.res` becomes the response. It throws if `context.finalized` is still false after composition (i.e., the chain never produced/awaited a response).
- `.route()` (sub-app mounting) also calls `compose([], app.errorHandler)(c, () => r.handler(c, next))` to wrap a sub-app's route handler so that the sub-app's own `errorHandler` applies when mounted into a parent app.
- `.use()` and the HTTP-method registration functions (`get`, `post`, etc.) all funnel through `#addRoute`, which pushes `[handler, RouterRoute]` into `this.router` (and `this.routes`) — this is what populates the array `compose` later iterates over. Multiple `.use()`/method calls on the same path accumulate as multiple middleware entries matched together at request time.

### Supporting pieces
- `src/context.ts` — defines `Context`, including `context.finalized`, `context.req.routeIndex` (set per-dispatch step in `compose`), and `context.res`/`context.error` used by the composer.
- `src/router.ts` — defines the `Router<T>.match()` contract that returns the ordered handler array `compose` consumes; actual router algorithms (`RegExpRouter`, `TrieRouter`, `SmartRouter`, etc.) live under `src/router/*` but are not part of composition itself, only matching.
- `src/utils/constants.ts` — exports `COMPOSED_HANDLER`, a symbol tagged onto a wrapped handler in `.route()` so introspection tools can find the original inner handler.

### Tests confirming behavior
`src/compose.test.ts` (present in the repo, not read in full here) contains the unit tests for `compose`'s onion-model behavior, `next()` double-call guard, and error propagation — I did not read its contents, so I can't cite specific test cases, only that it exists at that path.

### What I did not verify
- I did not read `src/compose.test.ts`'s contents.
- I did not inspect the actual router algorithm implementations under `src/router/*` (e.g. `reg-exp-router`, `trie-router`) — only confirmed the `Router` interface contract they must satisfy.
- I did not check `src/context.ts` line-by-line; I relied on symbol usage seen in `compose.ts`/`hono-base.ts` (`context.finalized`, `context.error`, `context.req.routeIndex`) rather than reading its full source.
- All fetched via `gh api repos/honojs/hono/contents/...` against the default branch at the time of this query (2026-07-05); I did not pin/verify a specific commit SHA.

import type { ContentfulStatusCode } from './utils/http-status'

/**
 * Options for creating an `HTTPException`.
 * @property res - Optional response object to use.
 * @property message - Optional custom error message.
 * @property cause - Optional cause of the error.
 */
type HTTPExceptionOptions = {
  res?: Response
  message?: string
  cause?: unknown
}

/**
 * `HTTPException` must be used when a fatal error such as authentication failure occurs.
 *
 * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/exception}
 *
 * @param {StatusCode} status - status code of HTTPException
 * @param {HTTPExceptionOptions} options - options of HTTPException
 * @param {HTTPExceptionOptions["res"]} options.res - response of options of HTTPException
 * @param {HTTPExceptionOptions["message"]} options.message - message of options of HTTPException
 * @param {HTTPExceptionOptions["cause"]} options.cause - cause of options of HTTPException
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * import { HTTPException } from 'hono/http-exception'
 *
 * // ...
 *
 * app.post('/auth', async (c, next) => {
 *   // authentication
 *   if (authorized === false) {
 *     throw new HTTPException(401, { message: 'Custom error message' })
 *   }
 *   await next()
 * })
 * ```
 */
export class HTTPException extends Error {
  readonly res?: Response
  readonly status: ContentfulStatusCode

    super(options?.message, { cause: options?.cause })
    this.res = options?.res
    this.status = status
